answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated runtime capacity at a central registrar to secure a unique identity, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent acts as a hollow node, anchoring its existence to a specific reservation of memory and compute time. A verifier probes the network for overlap; any attempt to share a structural timber of resources triggers an immediate prune. An opal shard of cryptographically signed duration proves occupancy.
